summary: Source decomposition of the Heegner-point Euler system from Howard's 'The Heegner point Kolyvagin system' (Sec. 0, Sec. 1.3, Secs. 1.5-1.7 and Sec. 2.3 read, including all proofs in Sec. 1.7 and in the proof of Thm. 1.6.5) together with Cornut-Vatsal's statements. Covers: the CM construction of h_m and P[m] with the Heegner hypothesis and the two excluded discriminants; the norm relation and the reduction congruence, and the two equivalent descriptions of the ideal I_ell = (a_ell, ell+1); the Selmer structure obtained by propagation, the transverse modification at primes dividing n, and Lemma 1.7.3's explicit vanishing computation ell(ell+1)/2 . c(Fr_lambda) = 0; the derived classes kappa-tilde_n with Lemma 1.7.1's proof, the descent to K through Hochschild-Serre (which is where full surjectivity is used), and McCallum's cocycle formula; Prop. 1.7.4's finite/singular automorphism chi_ell built from a_ell - (ell+1)Fr_ell, and Thm. 1.7.5's CORRECTED Kolyvagin system -- the raw derivative classes only ALMOST form one; hypotheses H.0-H.5 with H.4 and H.5 flagged as additional to Mazur-Rubin, Thm. 1.6.1, the full verification of H.0-H.5 for T_p(E), and Theorem A; the Lambda-adic construction with Lemma 2.3.4's two cases and Theorem B with its extra hypothesis p not dividing h_K, its DIVISIBILITY (not equality) conclusion, the Manin constant in Perrin-Riou's predicted equality, and the resulting rank inequality; and Cornut-Vatsal Thms. 1.4 and 1.5 with their exact hypotheses and the stated origin of the extra conditions in Thm. 1.5. HE.0, HE.7, HE.7s and HE.8b are not_read. Gross's paper -- the source of the norm relation and of the away-from-n local conditions -- is present in the library but has NO text layer.

nodes.title: The family of Heegner points h_m on X_0(N) and their images P[m] in E
nodes.statement: Let E/Q be an elliptic curve of conductor N and K an imaginary quadratic field of discriminant D prime to p, with D not -3 and not -4, such that every prime divisor of N is split in K (the Heegner hypothesis); assume in addition that p does not divide N. Fix an integral ideal a of O_K with O_K/a isomorphic to Z/NZ -- the Heegner hypothesis is exactly what makes such an a exist. For every integer m = p^k n with n a squarefree product of primes inert in K, let O_m be the order of conductor m in O_K and set h_m = [C/O_m -> C/(O_m intersect a)^{-1}], the cyclic N-isogeny of complex tori determined by the invertible O_m-ideal O_m intersect a. Then h_m is a point of X_0(N) rational over the ring class field K[m] of conductor m. Embedding X_0(N) into J_0(N) by sending the cusp at infinity to the origin and fixing a modular parametrisation J_0(N) -> E, the image P[m] in E(K[m]) is the Heegner point of conductor m.
hypotheses: the Heegner hypothesis is that ALL primes dividing N split in K; it is what produces the ideal a with O_K/a isomorphic to Z/NZ and hence the cyclic N-isogeny
D is prime to p and D is not -3 and not -4; the two excluded discriminants are the ones with extra units, and they are excluded for the whole of Howard's paper
p does not divide N
the base point for the embedding X_0(N) -> J_0(N) is the CUSP AT INFINITY; a different base point changes P[m] by a fixed class
the rationality of h_m over K[m] is the theory of complex multiplication applied to the pair (O_m, O_m intersect a); it is quoted, not proved, in the source read
the modular parametrisation is FIXED once and for all; the Manin constant c attached to this choice appears in the Perrin-Riou main conjecture but does not appear in Howard's Theorem A or B
proofSteps: Complex multiplication gives the pair of CM elliptic curves C/O_m and C/(O_m intersect a)^{-1} and the cyclic N-isogeny between them, hence a point of the moduli space X_0(N) over C.
The main theorem of complex multiplication identifies the field of definition of h_m as the ring class field K[m]; Howard states this without proof.
Sending the cusp at infinity to the origin gives the Abel-Jacobi embedding into J_0(N), and composing with the fixed parametrisation J_0(N) -> E gives P[m] in E(K[m]).
acceptance: Check that the ideal a exists exactly under the Heegner hypothesis, and that a different choice of a changes the family by an explicit Galois translation.
Check the case m = p^k n with k > 0, which is used in the anticyclotomic tower; the construction is stated for all such m, not only for squarefree n.
Check that the Manin constant enters only in the comparison with Perrin-Riou's module and NOT in the statements of Thms. A and B.
Check the two excluded discriminants D = -3, -4 and where the extra units would break the argument.

nodes.title: The Euler-system norm relation and the reduction congruence at inert auxiliary primes
nodes.statement: For n a squarefree product of primes inert in K and ell an inert prime with n*ell again admissible, the Heegner points satisfy the norm relation Norm_{K[n ell]/K[n]} P[n ell] = a_ell P[n], where a_ell is the trace of Frobenius at ell on T_p(E), and the reduction congruence P[n ell] is congruent to [Frobenius of lambda' in Gal(K[n ell]/Q)] applied to P[n], modulo lambda', for lambda' ANY prime of K[n ell] above ell. Here Gal(K[n]/K[m]) is isomorphic to the product over ell dividing n/m of G_ell, with G_ell = Gal(K[ell]/K[1]); and the ideal I_ell of Z_p is the smallest ideal containing ell + 1 for which Frobenius of the prime lambda above ell (equal to Fr_ell^2) acts trivially on T/I_ell T, so that Fr_ell acts on T/I_ell T with characteristic polynomial X^2 - 1; equivalently I_ell is generated by a_ell and ell + 1.
hypotheses: ell is inert in K and prime to p and to N (it lies in the set L = L_1(T) of Kolyvagin primes)
the norm relation is the trace from K[n ell] down to K[n] and produces the multiplier a_ell, NOT a_ell times a Frobenius; the Frobenius appears only in the congruence

the congruence holds modulo lambda' for ANY prime lambda' of K[n ell] above ell; it is a pointwise congruence between P[n ell] and a Frobenius translate of P[n], and is a genuinely stronger input than the trace relation alone
I_ell is defined by the trivial action of Fr_lambda = Fr_ell^2 on T/I_ell T, and is THEN shown to be generated by a_ell and ell + 1; the two descriptions must be kept aligned
proofSteps: Howard quotes both relations rather than proving them: the norm relation is attributed to Gross, 'Kolyvagin's work on modular elliptic curves', Proposition 3.7, or to Perrin-Riou Sec. 3.3; the congruence (13) is quoted in the same place.

The description of I_ell is derived in the source from the requirement that Fr_lambda act trivially on T/I_ell T: since Fr_ell has characteristic polynomial X^2 - a_ell X + ell on T and Fr_lambda = Fr_ell^2, the condition is exactly that a_ell and ell + 1 lie in I_ell.
The telescoping identity (sigma_ell - 1) D_ell = ell + 1 - Norm_ell, for D_ell the Kolyvagin derivative, is what converts the norm relation into the invariance statement of HE.4.
acceptance: Check that the norm relation is stated with a_ell and not with a_ell minus a Frobenius term; the shape of the Euler factor here differs from the cyclotomic and Kato cases.
Check that the congruence is used in the proof of Prop. 1.7.4 (the finite/singular comparison), and that it is NOT derivable from the norm relation.
Check the two descriptions of I_ell agree: the smallest ideal with Fr_lambda acting trivially on T/I_ell T, and the ideal (a_ell, ell + 1).

Check the initial conductor and unit exceptions: the source works throughout with D not -3, -4 and with n prime to N, so the exceptional small discriminants are excluded by hypothesis rather than treated.

sources.excerpt: If n ell in N we have the Euler system relation ([Gro91] Proposition 3.7, or [PR87] Section 3.3, for example) Norm_{K[n ell]/K[n]} P[n ell] = a_ell P[n] and the congruence (13) P[n ell] is congruent to [lambda'/(K[n ell]/Q)] P[n] (mod lambda') where lambda' is any prime of K[n ell] above ell.
sources.match: Gives both relations verbatim with their attributions, as recorded in the statement and proofSteps.

sources.excerpt: The ideal I_ell in Z_p is the smallest ideal containing ell + 1 for which Fr_lambda = Fr_ell^2 acts trivially on T/I_ell T, and hence on which Fr_ell acts with characteristic polynomial X^2 - 1. Therefore I_ell is generated by a_ell and ell + 1.
sources.match: Gives both descriptions of I_ell and the derivation of the second from the first.

sources.excerpt: Define the derivative operator D_ell in Z_p[G(ell)] by D_ell = sum_{i=1}^{ell} i sigma_ell^i, where sigma_ell is a fixed generator of G(ell), and let D_n = product over ell | n of D_ell in Z_p[G(n)]. One has the easy telescoping identity (sigma_ell - 1) D_ell = ell + 1 - Norm_ell.
sources.match: Gives the derivative operator and the telescoping identity that converts the norm relation into the invariance property.

nodes.title: Kummer classes of the Heegner points and the exact local conditions they satisfy
nodes.statement: Let F be the Selmer structure of Theorem 1.6.5 on T = T_p(E), so that H^1_F(K,T) = S_p(E/K): at every place v not dividing p the local condition is the unramified one, and at v dividing p it is obtained by propagating the image of the local Kummer map E(K_v) tensor Q_p -> H^1(K,V). For n a squarefree product of Kolyvagin primes, let H^1_{F(n)}(K, T/I_n T) be the generalised Selmer group of Definition 1.2.2, obtained from F by replacing the local condition at each prime of K dividing n by the TRANSVERSE one. Lemma 1.7.3: the derived class kappa_n lies in H^1_{F(n)}(K, T/I_n T). The proof splits into two parts: at places v not dividing n, the assertion loc_v(kappa_n) in H^1_F(K_v, T/I_n T) is Proposition 6.2 of Gross's paper (quoted, not proved); at a prime ell dividing n, with lambda the prime of K above ell and lambda' the unique prime of K[ell] above ell, one uses that lambda splits completely in K[n/ell] and hence lambda' splits completely in K[n], identifies K[ell]_{lambda'} = K[n]_{lambda''}, and computes (D_ell c)(Fr_lambda) = (sum_{i=1}^{ell} i) c(Fr_lambda) = [ell(ell+1)/2] c(Fr_lambda) = 0, because sigma_ell acts trivially on T/I_n T and ell + 1 lies in I_ell.
hypotheses: the transverse local condition at a prime dividing n is defined only for primes in the Kolyvagin set L, for which GK_v acts trivially on T/I_n T and the residue field order condition of Def. 1.1.8 holds
the vanishing computation uses ell(ell+1)/2 in Z_p; since ell is odd and ell + 1 lies in I_ell, the coefficient ell(ell+1)/2 lies in I_ell -- the halving is legitimate because p is ODD

the local condition at v dividing p is the PROPAGATED Bloch-Kato condition, and Howard records that propagation from V makes H^1(K_v,T)/H^1_F(K_v,T) torsion-free at every v, which is what gives hypothesis H.3
the identification H^1_F(K, E[p^infinity]) = Sel_{p^infinity}(E/K) is quoted from Rubin's Prop. 1.6.8
proofSteps: Define the Selmer structure F by propagation from V = T tensor Q_p, so that H^1_F(K,T) = S_p(E/K) and H^1_F(K,A) = Sel_{p^infinity}(E/K).
Modify F at the primes dividing n to the transverse condition, giving the generalised Selmer group H^1_{F(n)}.
Away from n, invoke Gross Prop. 6.2 for the local behaviour of the derived class.

At ell dividing n, reduce to a computation over the completion using the complete splitting of lambda in K[n/ell] and the identification K[ell]_{lambda'} = K[n]_{lambda''}, and conclude by Prop. 1.1.7 that it suffices to check (D_ell c)(Fr_lambda) = 0, which follows from the arithmetic of I_ell.
acceptance: Check the halving step ell(ell+1)/2: it is valid in Z_p because p is odd, and it is the only place where oddness of p enters this lemma.
Check that the local condition at v dividing p is the propagated one and not the naive unramified one; the two differ exactly at p.
Check that the assertion away from n is an IMPORT (Gross Prop. 6.2) and has not been proved here.
Check the component-group behaviour at bad primes: Howard's Selmer structure is defined by propagation, which sidesteps the component-group discussion that the stage text asks for.

sources.excerpt: Fix n in N and let F denote the Selmer structure of Theorem 1.6.5 on T, so that H^1_F(K, T) = S_p(E/K). Then kappa_n in H^1_{F(n)}(K, T/I_n T). Proof. The statement that loc_v(kappa_n) in H^1_F(K_v, T/I_n T) for v not dividing n is Proposition 6.2 of [Gro91].
sources.match: Gives the statement and records that the away-from-n part is imported from Gross.

sources.locator: Sec. 1.7, proof of Lemma 1.7.3, printed p. 20
sources.excerpt: The prime lambda of K above ell splits completely in K[n/ell], and so lambda' splits completely in K[n]. Fixing a prime lambda'' of K[n] above lambda', we have K[ell]_{lambda'} = K[n]_{lambda''}. ... By definition of I_n, the Frobenius automorphism, Fr_lambda in Gal(K_lambda^{unr}/K_lambda) acts trivially on T/I_n T, and so by Proposition 1.1.7 it suffices to show that (D_ell c)(Fr_lambda) in T/I_n T is zero. Since sigma_ell acts trivially on T/I_n T, we have (D_ell c)(Fr_lambda) = sum_{i=1}^{ell} i c(Fr_lambda) = [ell(ell+1)/2] c(Fr_lambda) = 0.
sources.match: Gives the splitting argument and the explicit vanishing computation, recorded in the statement and proofSteps.

sources.excerpt: let L be the condition at each place v of K which does not divide p, and at v|p take the image of the local Kummer map E(K_v) tensor Q_p -> H^1(K, V). Define local conditions on T_p(E) and E[p^infinity] isomorphic to V/T_p(E) by propagating F. By Proposition 1.6.8 of [Rub00], H^1_F(K, E[p^infinity]) = Sel_{p^infinity}(E/K).
sources.match: Gives the exact definition of the Selmer structure F and the identification of H^1_F with the classical Selmer group.

nodes.title: The derived classes kappa-tilde_n, their G(n)-invariance modulo I_n, and the descent to K
nodes.statement: For n a squarefree product of Kolyvagin primes put G(n) = Gal(K[n]/K) and G(n) = product over ell dividing n of G_ell, so that Gal(K[n]/K[m]) is isomorphic to G(n/m) for m dividing n. Choosing a set S of coset representatives for G(n) inside G(n), set kappa-tilde_n = sum over s in S of s D_n(P[n]) in E(K[n]). LEMMA 1.7.1: the image of kappa-tilde_n in E(K[n])/I_n E(K[n]) is fixed by G(n); the proof is the three-line computation (sigma_ell - 1) D_n P[n] = (sigma_ell - 1) D_ell D_{n/ell} P[n] = -D_{n/ell} Norm_ell P[n] = -a_ell D_{n/ell} P[n/ell], which vanishes modulo I_n because a_ell lies in I_ell which is contained in I_n. Since the surjectivity of G_K -> Aut(T) forces E(K[n])[p] = 0, the Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence makes restriction an ISOMORPHISM H^1(K, T/I_n T) -> H^1(K[n], T/I_n T)^{G(n)}, and kappa_n is defined as the unique preimage of delta_n(kappa-tilde_n) under it, delta_n being the Kummer map. LEMMA 1.7.2 gives kappa_n by the explicit cocycle kappa_n(sigma) = (sigma - 1)(kappa-tilde_n/p^{M_n}) - ((sigma-1) kappa-tilde_n)/p^{M_n}, where I_n = p^{M_n} Z_p, kappa-tilde_n/p^{M_n} is a fixed p^{M_n}-divisor in E(Kbar), and ((sigma-1)kappa-tilde_n)/p^{M_n} is the UNIQUE p^{M_n}-divisor of (sigma-1)kappa-tilde_n inside E(K[n]).
hypotheses: the surjectivity of G_K -> Aut_{Z_p}(T) is used HERE, to force E(K[n])[p] = 0 and hence to make the restriction map an isomorphism; without it the descent is not unrestricted and torsion invariants obstruct uniqueness
the invariance in Lemma 1.7.1 holds only MODULO I_n, not on the nose
the second term of the cocycle in Lemma 1.7.2 is the UNIQUE p^{M_n}-divisor inside E(K[n]); uniqueness again uses E(K[n])[p] = 0
the choice of the coset representatives S and of the generators sigma_ell are choices; the transformation law under changing sigma_ell is what forces the tensor factor G_n in the Kolyvagin system
Lemma 1.7.2 is attributed to McCallum, Lemma 4.1
proofSteps: Compute (sigma_ell - 1) D_n P[n] using the telescoping identity of HE.2 and the norm relation, obtaining -a_ell D_{n/ell} P[n/ell]; since a_ell is in I_ell it vanishes modulo I_n.
Use E(K[n])[p] = 0 (a consequence of surjectivity) and Hochschild-Serre to identify H^1(K, T/I_n T) with the G(n)-invariants of H^1(K[n], T/I_n T).
Define kappa_n as the unique preimage of the Kummer image of kappa-tilde_n, and record the explicit cocycle of Lemma 1.7.2 (quoted from McCallum).
At n = 1, kappa_1 is the Kummer image of Norm_{K[1]/K} P[1] in H^1(K,T).
acceptance: Check that the invariance is modulo I_n and that a claim of exact invariance would be false.
Check where E(K[n])[p] = 0 is used: in the descent isomorphism AND in the uniqueness of the p^{M_n}-divisor of Lemma 1.7.2. A weaker large-image hypothesis must address both.
Check the transformation law of kappa_n under a change of the generator sigma_ell, which is why the Kolyvagin system takes values in H^1 tensor G_n.
Check the n = 1 case against the statement that kappa_1 is the Kummer image of the norm of P[1] and is nonzero exactly when the Heegner point is non-torsion.

sources.locator: Sec. 1.7, Lemma 1.7.1 and its proof, printed pp. 19-20
sources.excerpt: Choosing a set of coset representatives S for G(n) in G(n), we define kappa-tilde_n = sum_{s in S} s D_n(P[n]) in E(K[n]). Lemma 1.7.1. The image of kappa-tilde_n in E(K[n])/I_n E(K[n]) is fixed by G(n). Proof. For each ell|n we have the equalities in E(K[n])/I_n E(K[n]) (sigma_ell - 1)D_n(P[n]) = (sigma_ell - 1)D_ell D_{n/ell} P[n] = -D_{n/ell} Norm_ell(P[n]) = -a_ell D_{n/ell}(P[n/ell]). Since a_ell in I_ell contained in I_n, the claim follows.
sources.match: Gives the construction and the complete proof of the invariance modulo I_n.

sources.excerpt: Our assumption that the map G_K -> Aut(T) is surjective guarantees that E(K[n])[p] = 0, and so, by the Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence, restriction gives an isomorphism H^1(K, T/I_n T) -> H^1(K[n], T/I_n T)^{G(n)}. If delta_n : E(K[n])/I_n E(K[n]) -> H^1(K[n], T/I_n T) is the Kummer map, we define kappa_n to be the unique preimage of delta_n(kappa-tilde_n) under restriction.
sources.match: States exactly where the surjectivity hypothesis is used and how the descent to K is performed.

sources.excerpt: Lemma 1.7.2. The class kappa_n in H^1(K, T/I_n T) may be given as an explicit cocycle as follows. Let I_n = p^{M_n} Z_p and fix a p^{M_n}-divisor of kappa-tilde_n, kappa-tilde_n/p^{M_n} in E(Kbar). For sigma in G_K let ((sigma-1)kappa-tilde_n)/p^{M_n} be the unique p^{M_n}-divisor of (sigma - 1)kappa-tilde_n in E(K[n]). Then kappa_n(sigma) = (sigma - 1)(kappa-tilde_n/p^{M_n}) - ((sigma - 1)kappa-tilde_n)/p^{M_n}. Proof. This is Lemma 4.1 of [Mc91].
sources.match: Gives the explicit cocycle and its attribution.

nodes.title: The finite/singular comparison chi_ell and the corrected Kolyvagin system
nodes.statement: PROPOSITION 1.7.4: for every ell dividing lambda in L there is an AUTOMORPHISM chi_ell : T/I_ell T -> T/I_ell T such that, for n ell in the admissible set, chi_ell(kappa_n(Fr_lambda)) = kappa_{n ell}(sigma_ell) as elements of T/I_{n ell} T. The map is constructed as the composite E(K_lambda) -> E-tilde(Fbar) -> E-tilde(F)[p^infinity] --(p^{-M_ell}(a_ell - (ell+1) Fr_ell))--> E-tilde(F)[I_ell] -> E[I_ell], where the first arrow is reduction at lambda, the second is projection to the p-Sylow subgroup, and the last is the canonical lift; it is surjective because the action of Fr_ell splits the p-Sylow subgroup of E-tilde(F) into cyclic eigencomponents whose lengths are the p-orders of ell + 1 - a_ell and ell + 1 + a_ell, and since E[I_ell] is defined over K_lambda it factors through an isomorphism E(K_lambda)/I_ell E(K_lambda) -> E[I_ell], which under E(K_lambda)/I_ell E(K_lambda) = H^1(K_lambda^{unr}/K_lambda, E[I_ell]) = E[I_ell] gives the automorphism. Hence the raw classes kappa_n only ALMOST form a Kolyvagin system. THEOREM 1.7.5: there is a genuine Kolyvagin system kappa' for (T, F, L) with kappa'_1 = kappa_1, obtained by setting kappa'_n = chi_n^{-1}(kappa_n) tensor (tensor over ell dividing n of sigma_ell) in H^1_{F(n)}(K, T/I_n T) tensor G_n, where chi_n is the composite of the pairwise commuting automorphisms chi_ell.
hypotheses: the correction is by an automorphism of T/I_ell T constructed from the reduction map and the operator a_ell - (ell+1) Fr_ell; it is NOT the identity, so the raw derivative classes do not satisfy Mazur-Rubin's relations
the surjectivity of chi_ell uses the eigencomponent structure of the p-Sylow subgroup of E-tilde(F) under Fr_ell, whose lengths are ord_p(ell + 1 - a_ell) and ord_p(ell + 1 + a_ell)
the factorisation through E(K_lambda)/I_ell E(K_lambda) uses that E[I_ell] is defined over K_lambda, which is exactly the defining property of the Kolyvagin primes
the chi_ell pairwise commute, which is what makes chi_n well defined
the tensor factor G_n = tensor over ell dividing n of G_ell records the dependence on the chosen generators sigma_ell
proofSteps: Use Lemma 1.7.2's cocycle description together with the Euler system relation and the reduction congruence (13) of HE.2 to obtain kappa_{n ell}(sigma_ell) congruent to [(a_ell - (ell+1) Fr_ell)/p^{M_{n ell}}] kappa-tilde_n modulo lambda'; Howard refers to the proof of Proposition 4.4 of McCallum.
Define chi_ell as the displayed composite and prove surjectivity via the Fr_ell-eigencomponent decomposition of the p-Sylow subgroup of E-tilde(F).
Factor chi_ell through E(K_lambda)/I_ell E(K_lambda) and identify that quotient with E[I_ell] via unramified cohomology, obtaining an automorphism.
Define kappa'_n = chi_n^{-1}(kappa_n) tensor sigma_ell's; the resulting family satisfies the Kolyvagin system relations of Definition 1.2.3 and agrees with kappa_1 at n = 1.
acceptance: Check that the correction is genuinely needed: Howard says explicitly that the kappa_n 'almost form a Kolyvagin system. Only a slight modification is needed.' Asserting that raw derivative classes form a Kolyvagin system would be an error.
Check that the reduction congruence (13) -- not merely the norm relation -- is what produces the operator a_ell - (ell+1) Fr_ell.
Check the commutation of the chi_ell and that chi_1 is the identity so that kappa'_1 = kappa_1.

nodes.title: The abstract bound (Thm. 1.6.1) with hypotheses H.0-H.5, and Kolyvagin's Theorem A
nodes.statement: Let R be a discrete valuation ring with uniformiser pi, (T,F,L) a Selmer triple satisfying HYPOTHESES H.0-H.5, and L_s(T) contained in L for s large. THEOREM 1.6.1: if there is a Kolyvagin system kappa in KS(T,F,L) with kappa_1 nonzero, then H^1_F(K,T) is a FREE RANK-ONE R-module and there is a FINITE R-module M with H^1_F(K,A) isomorphic to D + M + M, and length_R(M) <= length_R(H^1_F(K,T)/R kappa_1). The hypotheses are: H.0 T is free of rank 2 over R; H.1 T-bar is an absolutely irreducible (R/m)[[G_K]]-representation; H.2 there is a Galois extension F/Q containing K with G_F acting trivially on T and H^1(F(mu_{p^infinity})/K, T-bar) = 0; H.3 at every v in Sigma(F) the local condition is cartesian on Quot(T); H.4 there is a perfect symmetric R-bilinear pairing T x T -> R(1) with (s^sigma, t^{tau sigma tau^{-1}}) = (s,t)^sigma, and F is its OWN EXACT ORTHOGONAL COMPLEMENT under the induced local pairing H^1(K_v,T) x H^1(K_v-bar,T) -> R at every v; H.5 (a) the G_K-action on T-bar extends to G_Q and tau splits T-bar into one-dimensional eigenspaces, (b) F propagated to T-bar is G_Q-stable, (c) the residual pairing satisfies (s^tau,t^tau) = (s,t)^tau. THEOREM 1.6.5 (Kolyvagin) specialises this to T = T_p(E) and yields THEOREM A: assuming p odd, p, D and N pairwise coprime, and G_K -> Aut_{Z_p}(T) SURJECTIVE, if kappa_1 is nonzero then S_p(E/K) is free of rank one over Z_p and Sel_{p^infinity}(E/K) is isomorphic to (Q_p/Z_p) + M + M with length_{Z_p}(M) <= length_{Z_p}(S_p(E/K)/Z_p kappa_1).
hypotheses: H.4 -- the self-duality of T up to a twist, with F its own exact orthogonal complement -- is NOT one of Mazur-Rubin's hypotheses; Howard states that it 'plays an essential role here'. H.5 is introduced 'to overcome a technical difficulty'

Theorem A's standing hypotheses are p ODD, the pairwise coprimality of p, D and N, and the SURJECTIVITY of G_K -> Aut_{Z_p}(T) onto the full automorphism group; together with the standing D not -3, -4 and the Heegner hypothesis of HE.1

the conclusion gives one DIVISIBLE rank-one summand and two paired finite summands M; the factor of two in the length of the discrete Selmer group is a consequence of the self-duality H.4 and is not an artefact

the bound is an inequality (a divisibility of lengths), with the index of the bottom class kappa_1 on the right; equality requires the stronger primitivity hypotheses of the abstract theory and is NOT asserted here

in the verification of H.2 the extension F = K(E[p^infinity]) works because surjectivity gives H^1(GL_2(Z_p), F_p^2) = 0, proved by inflation-restriction applied to the diagonally embedded mu_{p-1} inside GL_2(Z_p) -- this is where p - 1 > 1, i.e. p odd, is used
H.3 holds because F is obtained by PROPAGATION from V, which makes H^1(K_v,T)/H^1_F(K_v,T) torsion-free at every place (Mazur-Rubin Lemma 3.7.1)

the nonvanishing of the bottom class is an ANALYTIC input, not part of this theorem: Howard records in Sec. 0 that 'the celebrated theorem of Gross and Zagier says that ord_{s=1} L(s,E/K) = 1 iff kappa_1 has infinite order', and immediately after Thm. 1.7.5 that kappa'_1 'is nonzero provided that L'(E/K,1) not= 0, by the results of Gross' and Zagier. Theorem A is vacuous without it
proofSteps: Theorem 1.6.1 is proved by a sequence of lemmas reducing modulo m^k, using the decomposition H^1_{F(n)}(K,T^{(k)}) = R^{(k),epsilon} + M^{(k)}(n) + M^{(k)}(n) with epsilon independent of n and k, and Prop. 1.5.9 controlling how the localisation vanishing propagates when a prime is added; the full proof was read only in outline.

Theorem 1.6.5 is proved by verifying H.0-H.5 for T_p(E) with the propagated Selmer structure: H.0 trivially; H.1 from surjectivity; H.2 with F = K(E[p^infinity]) via the GL_2(Z_p)-cohomology vanishing; H.3 from propagation plus Mazur-Rubin Lemma 3.7.1; H.4 by the Weil pairing with the twist of Remark 1.3.2, whose orthogonality relations are equivalent to Tate local duality; H.5 using that E is defined over Q, with (a) from tau-invariance of the Weil pairing, (b) from G_Q-stability of the local Kummer images, and (c) from (s^tau,t^tau) = e(s^tau,t) = e(s,t^tau)^tau = (s,t)^tau.
Theorem A follows by applying Theorem 1.6.5 to the Kolyvagin system kappa' of HE.5.
acceptance: Check that H.4 and H.5 are recorded whenever Theorem 1.6.1 is invoked; they are not part of the Mazur-Rubin package.

Check the three separate arithmetic hypotheses of Theorem A -- p odd, pairwise coprimality, full surjectivity -- and do not conflate surjectivity with residual surjectivity or with residual irreducibility.
Check the direction of the divisibility and the factor of two: the discrete Selmer group has ONE divisible summand and TWO copies of the same finite M.
Check that the conclusion is an inequality; ES.5-style equality requires primitivity, which is not proved here.
Check the Weil-pairing verification of H.4 including the twist of Remark 1.3.2, since an untwisted pairing does not satisfy the stated equivariance.

Check that the hypothesis 'kappa_1 not= 0' is discharged by a Gross-Zagier statement and not by the construction; at finite level that is ord_{s=1} L(s,E/K) = 1, and in the tower it is Cornut-Vatsal (see HE.8 and HE.8c).

If kappa_1 not= 0 then S_p(E/K) is free of rank one over Z_p and there is a finite Z_p-module M such that Sel_{p^infinity}(E/K) is isomorphic to (Q_p/Z_p) + M + M with length_{Z_p}(M) <= length_{Z_p}(S_p(E/K)/Z_p kappa_1).

sources.excerpt: Hypothesis H.1 follows from our assumption that G_K surjects onto Aut_{Z_p}(T_p(E)). This assumption also implies that H^1(K(E[p^infinity])/K, E[p]) isomorphic to H^1(GL2(Z_p), F_p^2) = 0 (for the second equality, apply the inflation-restriction sequence to the subgroup mu_{p-1} contained in GL2(Z_p) embedded diagonally.) Hence H.2 holds with F = K(E[p^infinity]). The fact that F is obtained by propagation from V implies that the quotient of H^1(K_v, T_p(E)) by H^1_F(K_v, T_p(E)) is torsion-free for every place v, and hence Hypothesis H.3 holds by Lemma 3.7.1 of [MR04]. The pairing of H.4 is the Weil pairing, modified as in Remark 1.3.2.

The class kappa'_1 is the image of Norm_{K[1]/K} P[1] under the Kummer map E(K) -> H^1(K,T), and so is nonzero provided that L'(E/K,1) not= 0, by the results of Gross [and Zagier].

nodes.title: The anticyclotomic Lambda-adic Heegner Kolyvagin system and Howard's Theorem B
nodes.statement: Assume in addition that E is ORDINARY at p. Let K_infinity be the anticyclotomic Z_p-extension of K, Gamma = Gal(K_infinity/K), Lambda = Z_p[[Gamma]], K_n the subfield with [K_n:K] = p^n, T isomorphic to T tensor Lambda and A isomorphic to Hom(T, mu_{p^infinity}). Greenberg-style generalised Selmer groups H^1_{F_Lambda}(K,T) inside lim H^1(K_n,T) and H^1_{F_Lambda}(K,A) inside colim H^1(K_n,E[p^infinity]) are pseudo-isomorphic to lim S_p(E/K_n) and colim Sel_{p^infinity}(E/K_n) respectively; set X = Hom(H^1_{F_Lambda}(K,A), Q_p/Z_p). A compatible family Q[n] of Lambda-adic Heegner classes is constructed by a compactness argument, derivative operators D_n in Z_p[G(n)] inside Lambda[G(n)] are applied to give kappa-tilde_n = sum over s in S of s D_n Q[n], and kappa_n is defined as the unique preimage under H^1(K, T/I_n T) -> H^1(K[n], T/I_n T)^{G(n)}, the bijectivity following from H^0(K[n], T/I_n T) = lim H^0(K_k[n], E[I_n]) = 0 since E has no p-torsion over any abelian extension of K. LEMMA 2.3.4 shows kappa_n lies in H^1_{F_Lambda(n)}(K, T/I_n T). Its proof has FOUR parts, not two. At primes dividing n the localisation lies in the transverse subspace 'exactly as in the proof of Lemma 1.7.3'. Case (i), v not dividing pN: H^1_{F_Lambda}(K_v, T/I_n T) equals the unramified subgroup, because Gal(K_v^{unr}/K_v) has cohomological dimension one, and the Kummer image is unramified by the injectivity of torsion points in the reduction of E. Case (ii), v dividing N: the Heegner hypothesis forces the prime w to be FINITELY DECOMPOSED in K_infinity[n], Rubin's Prop. B.3.4 gives H^1(K_v,T) = H^1_unr(K_v,T), and the required injectivity reduces, by local duality and Shapiro's lemma, to the surjectivity of a norm map on p-power torsion, which holds because the degree of K_infinity[n]_{w'} over K_{infinity,v'} is prime to p. Case (iii), v dividing p -- the longest, and omitted from the first draft of this node: one sets Fil_w(T) = ker(T -> T_p(E-tilde)) and gr_w(T) = T/Fil_w(T), shows that the image of delta(n) lands in the ordinary subgroup H^1_ord(K[n]_w, T) because a universal norm would yield a class in the p-adic Tate module of the FINITE group E-tilde(F[n])[p^infinity], which is trivial, and then lifts loc_v(kappa_n) to H^1(K_v, T^+/I_n T^+) by a diagram chase whose relevant kernel is an inverse limit that vanishes. THEOREM 2.3.7 states that the Lambda-module H is free of rank one, generated by kappa-tilde_1; its proof is NOT self-contained -- 'by the main result of [Cor02], one of the points Norm_{K_k[1]/K_k} P_k[1] has infinite order, and so Proposition 10 of section 3 of [PR87] implies that H is free of rank one' -- so Cornut's nontriviality theorem and Perrin-Riou's proposition are both imports, and the hypothesis p not dividing h_K enters there as the statement that G(1), the ideal class group of K, has no p-torsion. THEOREM B: with the hypotheses of Theorem A, E ordinary at p, and p NOT DIVIDING THE CLASS NUMBER OF K, the module H^1_{F_Lambda}(K,T) is torsion-free of rank one and there is a finitely generated torsion Lambda-module M with (a) char(M) = char(M)^iota for iota the involution induced by inversion in Gamma, (b) X pseudo-isomorphic to Lambda + M + M, and (c) char(M) divides char(H^1_{F_Lambda}(K,T)/H).
hypotheses: E ordinary at p, and p does NOT divide the class number h_K of K; the latter is an extra hypothesis of Theorem B beyond those of Theorem A, and carrying a class-number factor in a construction does not remove it
the class kappa^{Hg}_1 is nonzero BY THE WORK OF CORNUT AND VATSAL; this is an imported analytic/geometric nonvanishing input, not a formal consequence of the inverse limit

conclusion (c) is a DIVISIBILITY, not an equality; Perrin-Riou's conjecture predicts char(M) = c^{-1} char(H^1_{F_Lambda}(K,T)/H) with c the Manin constant of the chosen modular parametrisation, and Howard proves only one divisibility
the identification of H with Perrin-Riou's module is itself part of the content of Thm. 2.3.7
the source notes that parts (a) and (b) were already known from Bertolini, Cornut and Nekovar; only (c) is new

the reduction of a Kolyvagin system for T at a height-one prime P of Lambda is to a Kolyvagin system for T tensor_Lambda S_P with S_P the integral closure of Lambda/P; the machinery of Theorem A is then applied prime by prime

Theorem 2.3.7, which identifies H as free of rank one and is what makes Theorem B non-vacuous, imports Cornut's nontriviality theorem [Cor02] and Perrin-Riou's Prop. 10 of [PR87, Sec. 3]; neither is proved by Howard, and p not dividing h_K is used in its proof through the absence of p-torsion in the ideal class group of K
proofSteps: Construct the compatible family Q[n] by lifting Phi x to the inverse limit H-tilde of the modules H-tilde_k and pushing forward along phi(m); compactness of the module of partial families gives non-emptiness of the inverse limit over all n.
Apply the derivative operators and descend exactly as in Sec. 1.7, using H^0(K[n], T/I_n T) = 0.

Prove the local conditions by Lemma 2.3.4: the transverse part exactly as in Lemma 1.7.3; case (i) using cd(Gal(K_v^{unr}/K_v)) = 1 and the injectivity of torsion in the reduction; case (ii) using the finite decomposition forced by the Heegner hypothesis together with Rubin Prop. B.3.4 and a prime-to-p degree argument; and case (iii), v | p, using the ordinary filtration Fil_w(T) and the finiteness of E-tilde(F[n])[p^infinity].
Reduce at each height-one prime P of Lambda and apply the same machinery as for Theorem A; assemble the resulting bounds into (a), (b), (c).

Via Mazur's control theorem, rank_{Z_p} X/(gamma-1)X = corank_{Z_p} Sel_{p^infinity}(E/K), so (b) makes that corank ODD, consistent with the Heegner hypothesis forcing sign -1; and (c) plus control gives rank_{Z_p} S_p(E/K) <= 1 + 2 ord_J(L) with J the augmentation ideal and L = char(H^1_{F_Lambda}(K,T)/H). Howard notes that equality is NOT typically expected.
acceptance: Check that p not dividing h_K is carried; it is a hypothesis of Theorem B only.
Check that the nonvanishing of kappa^{Hg}_1 is an import from Cornut-Vatsal and is NOT deduced from the construction.
Check that (c) is one divisibility and that Perrin-Riou's equality involves the Manin constant c.
Check the inequality rank_{Z_p} S_p(E/K) <= 1 + 2 ord_J(L) and Howard's own remark that equality is not typically expected.

Check all three local cases of Lemma 2.3.4, not only the first two: the Heegner hypothesis reappears in case (ii) to force finite decomposition in K_infinity[n], and case (iii) at v | p needs the ordinary filtration and is where the good-ordinary hypothesis does its work in the local verification.

Let H denote the Lambda-submodule of H^1_{F_Lambda}(K, T) generated by kappa^{Hg}_1, and let iota : Lambda -> Lambda be the involution induced by inversion in Gamma. The Lambda-module H^1_{F_Lambda}(K, T) is torsion-free of rank one, and there is a finitely-generated torsion Lambda-module M such that (a) char(M) = char(M)^iota (b) X pseudo-isomorphic to Lambda + M + M (c) char(M) divides char(H^1_{F_Lambda}(K, T)/H).

nodes.title: Cornut-Vatsal nonvanishing: the exact statements and their hypotheses
nodes.statement: Let F be totally real, K/F a CM extension, pi a cuspidal automorphic representation, P a prime, omega the central character. Let K[P^n]/K be the abelian extension attached by class field theory to K^x K_infinity^x (O-hat_{P^n})^x inside A_K^x, so that G(n) = Gal(K[P^n]/K) is isomorphic to Pic(O_{P^n}); put K[P^infinity] = union K[P^n], G(infinity) = lim G(n), G_0 the TORSION subgroup of G(infinity). It is shown that G_0 is finite and G(infinity)/G_0 is a free Z_p-module of rank [F_P : Q_p]; the reciprocity map of K sends A_F^x into a subgroup G_2 isomorphic to Pic(O_F) of G_0, and the compatibility condition on chi becomes chi . omega = 1 on G_2. For a character chi_0 of G_0 with chi_0 . omega = 1 on A_F^x, let P(n,chi_0) be the set of characters of G(n) inducing chi_0 on G_0 and NOT factoring through G(n-1). THEOREM 1.4 (definite case): for the data (pi,K,P) definite and any chi_0 of G_0 with chi_0 . omega = 1 on A_F^x, for ALL n SUFFICIENTLY LARGE there EXISTS chi in P(n,chi_0) with L(pi,chi,1/2) nonzero. THEOREM 1.5 (indefinite case, slightly more restrictive): assume in addition that omega = 1 and that N, D and P are PAIRWISE COPRIME; then for any chi_0 of G_0 with chi_0 = 1 on A_F^x, for all n sufficiently large there exists chi in P(n,chi_0) with L'(pi,chi,1/2) nonzero.
hypotheses: in the definite case the source assumes throughout that the pair (pi,K) is NOT EXCEPTIONAL. 'Exceptional' is DEFINED in Def. 1.3 by pi isomorphic to pi tensor eta; the double zero is the MOTIVATION, not the definition. The source explains that this occurs precisely when pi is isomorphic to pi(alpha) for a quasi-character alpha of A_K^x/K^x, in which case L(pi,chi,s) = L(alpha chi, s) L(alpha chi_0, s) with chi_0 the outer twist by Gal(K/F), each factor has a functional equation with sign +-1, and 'it can and does happen that both signs are -1', giving at least a double zero

Theorem 1.5 has the two EXTRA hypotheses omega = 1 and N, D, P pairwise coprime; the authors state these 'are due to the fact that these formulae are not yet known in full generality' -- i.e. they come from the availability of the Gross-Zagier formula, not from the CM-point argument
the conclusion is EXISTENCE of a nonvanishing character in each sufficiently large conductor stratum with the prescribed torsion type chi_0, NOT nonvanishing for every sufficiently ramified character
the characters range over P(n,chi_0): they induce chi_0 on the torsion subgroup G_0 and do NOT factor through G(n-1), i.e. they have exact conductor P^n
the authors state that they prove the relevant statements ABOUT CM POINTS without the extra restrictions; only the passage to L-values needs them
proofSteps: The proof reduces nonvanishing of L-functions and their derivatives to nontriviality of certain CM points via Gross-Zagier formulae: in the general framework there is a discrete set of CM points with a continuous Galois action and a function psi such that chi is generic exactly when the twisted integral a(x,chi) = integral over Gal^{ab}_K of chi(sigma) psi(sigma . x) d sigma is nonzero.
The geometric input is a CM-point equidistribution statement, which the authors prove without the extra hypotheses; the extra hypotheses enter only when converting it into an L-value statement.

Each theorem is reduced to a CM-point statement. For Thm. 1.4 the source says 'Theorem 1.4 therefore is a consequence of the following result'; for Thm. 1.5 it says 'Zhang's Gross-Zagier formula implies that Theorem 1.5 is now a consequence of the following result', namely Thm. 1.10 -- for any good CM point x of conductor P^n with n sufficiently large there exists chi in P(n,chi_0) with a(x,chi) nonzero -- 'which itself is a special case of Theorem 4.1 in the text'. None of Thms. 1.10, 4.1 or the corresponding definite-case statement was read here.
acceptance: Check that the conclusion is an existence statement in each large conductor stratum with the FIXED torsion type chi_0; a statement that all sufficiently ramified characters are nonvanishing is stronger and is not proved.

Lemma 1.7.3 and its complete proof match, including the import of Gross Prop. 6.2 for the places away from n, the complete splitting of lambda in K[n/ell], the identification K[ell]_{lambda'} = K[n]_{lambda''}, the appeal to Prop. 1.1.7 and the computation ell(ell+1)/2 . c(Fr_lambda) = 0. The definition of the Selmer structure F before Thm. 1.6.5, with the local Kummer image at v | p and Rubin's Prop. 1.6.8, also matches.

Lemma 1.7.1 with its three-line proof, the sentence locating exactly where surjectivity is used ('guarantees that E(K[n])[p] = 0, and so, by the Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence, restriction gives an isomorphism'), and Lemma 1.7.2's explicit cocycle with its attribution to Lemma 4.1 of [Mc91] are all verbatim.

Prop. 1.7.4, its proof (the congruence for kappa_{n ell}(sigma_ell), the composite defining chi_ell, the Fr_ell-eigencomponent argument for surjectivity with the orders of ell+1-a_ell and ell+1+a_ell, the factorisation through E(K_lambda)/I_ell E(K_lambda) and the unramified identification) and Thm. 1.7.5 with the remark that the raw classes 'almost form a Kolyvagin system' are all verbatim. The node is right that the correction is essential.

H.0-H.5 are verbatim, as are the remark that H.4 'is not used by those authors, but plays an essential role here' and that H.5 overcomes a technical difficulty, Thm. 1.6.1, Thm. 1.6.5 with its complete verification (the inflation-restriction argument with mu_{p-1} diagonal in GL_2(Z_p), Lemma 3.7.1 of [MR04], the Weil pairing modified as in Remark 1.3.2, and the three parts of H.5), Prop. 1.5.9, and Theorem A. Extended in review: the node did not record that the hypothesis kappa_1 not= 0 is discharged by Gross-Zagier -- Howard states in Sec. 0 that kappa_1 has infinite order if and only if ord_{s=1} L(s,E/K) = 1, and after Thm. 1.7.5 that kappa'_1 is nonzero provided L'(E/K,1) is nonzero. Without that, Theorem A is vacuous, so it belongs in the hypotheses.

Theorem B with all its hypotheses and three conclusions, the Perrin-Riou main conjecture with the Manin constant, the inequality (1) with 'one does not typically expect equality', the remark that (a) and (b) were already known from Bertolini, Cornut and Nekovar, the reduction at height-one primes, and the compactness construction of the family Q[n] are all verbatim. Two corrections. Lemma 2.3.4's proof has FOUR parts, not the two recorded: the transverse part at primes dividing n, case (i) v not dividing pN, case (ii) v | N, and case (iii) v | p -- the last being the longest, using the ordinary filtration Fil_w(T) and the finiteness of E-tilde(F[n])[p^infinity]. And Thm. 2.3.7 is not self-contained: its proof imports Cornut's main result and Perrin-Riou's Prop. 10, and it is there that p not dividing h_K is used, as the absence of p-torsion in the class group.

Thms. 1.4 and 1.5 are verbatim, as are the structure of G(infinity) and G_0, the subgroup G_2 isomorphic to Pic(O_F), the definition of P(n,chi_0), and the authors' statement that Thm. 1.5's extra hypotheses exist only because the Gross-Zagier formulae 'are not yet known in full generality'. Correction: 'exceptional' is DEFINED by pi isomorphic to pi tensor eta (Def. 1.3); the double-zero factorisation is the motivation for excluding such pairs, not the definition. Extended: Thm. 1.5 is reduced, via Zhang's Gross-Zagier formula, to Thm. 1.10 (a special case of the paper's Thm. 4.1), which is the CM-point statement; neither was read.
